[AI engineering](../index.qmd) / Evaluation and error analysis

Turn “it seems good” into a repeatable account of what works, what fails and what changed.

## What to understand

- **Task definition:** desired behavior, unacceptable failures and whose judgment matters.
- **Dataset design:** representative inputs, edge cases, held-out examples, provenance and leakage control.
- **Error analysis:** inspect real failures, group causes and choose a change that targets one cause.
- **Scoring:** deterministic assertions, expert rubrics and calibrated model judges with human checks.
- **Agent and RAG evaluation:** inspect retrieved evidence, tool calls, permissions and trajectories.
- **Experiment design:** compare versions on the same cases; examine subgroup failures, uncertainty, cost and latency.
- **Feedback:** production incidents and user corrections become new regression cases.

## How the pieces connect

Evaluation sits around the entire build loop. A failure in retrieval needs a different fix from a permission bug, unclear task or weak model.

## A question to test

Create a small versioned task set and a rubric. Run two implementations against it, manually inspect disagreements, and write why you would keep one.

**Platform note, 25 November 2026:** evaluation is a practice, separate from a hosted product. OpenAI’s hosted Evals surfaces are retiring; consult [the current notice](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations) and use a maintained evaluation workflow.
